title: Functions that take functions
description:
Write three functions:

```javascript
function average(...numbers) { }          // the average of any number of arguments; 0 when there are none
function applyTimes(f, times, start) { }  // f applied `times` times: applyTimes(x => x * 2, 3, 1) is 8
function compose(...fns) { }              // a function that applies fns right to left: compose(f, g)(x) is f(g(x))
```

`compose()` with no functions returns a function that gives back its argument unchanged.
hints: A rest parameter `...numbers` is a real array, so `length` and a `for...of` loop work on it.
`compose` returns a new arrow function. Inside it, start with `value = x` and loop over `fns` from the last index down to 0, applying each function in turn: `value = fns[i](value)`.
stretch: Write `pipe(...fns)`, which applies them left to right instead.
